scenario.title: Dedicated Test Machines from zero
situations: Existing host without a reset baseline
Several OS targets or multiple simultaneous hosts
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
scenario.review: Older research may describe heavier onboarding. Apply minimum activation and optional-adoption boundaries first.
questions: This audit read setup contracts and CLI help, not live OS/vendor readiness. Per-OS steps require actual fixture proof.
Whether every external fixture should require the present standard Claude/Codex/Cursor probes is a product scope question, separate from FIRST-USER current-harness readiness.

lessons.title: Distinguish local browser from dedicated machine
lessons.when: A case needs a browser, OS state, real terminal or fresh install
lessons.need: Local browser capture can use packaged browser setup without a Test Machine. Machine methods require a registered project host; the Machine QA Pack supplies methods and recipes, not infrastructure or credentials.
lessons.surface: Public QA browser section; Machine QA Pack README; JOURNEYS row 13.
lessons.gap: The public QA page lacks a clear from-zero Test Machine entry. Proposed row 13 should select local browser versus dedicated host before recommending setup.

lessons.title: Follow the installed OS-specific procedure
lessons.when: User agrees that dedicated machine coverage is needed
lessons.need: Use the installed Pack version: dedicated account/network, named test-machine settings, workstation-local SSH/desktop secrets, required tools/sign-ins and effective desktop permissions. Supported recipes cover macOS, Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows through WSL2; native Windows Yoke is not this fixture.
lessons.surface: Pack README → host-provisioning → per-OS procedure; settings contract.
lessons.gap: Setup support exists; improve discovery instead of building another provisioner. Keep project-specific infrastructure/accounts and private fixture policy out of a universal user recipe.

lessons.title: Choose starting-state and prove reset deliberately
lessons.when: Before scheduling QA that resets a host
lessons.need: A dedicated baseline needs golden capture plus restore proof, not just SSH or a saved archive. Verify/reset are destructive provisioning operations. No baseline is also a supported no-reset posture; an as_is case needs a reason. Capacity-machine registration is separate from test-machine registration.
lessons.surface: Per-OS capture/verify/reset; machine setting optional baseline; Pack starting-state contract.
lessons.gap: The entry guide must explain when a resettable rig is necessary. Do not make every browser user build a clean-install lab or mistake capacity registration for QA readiness.

lessons.title: Name the missing setup and resume point
lessons.when: Machine absent, ambiguous, leased, low on disk or desktop/auth proof fails
lessons.need: Use registered get/list and exact OS recovery. Wait for a live host lease; preserve private baselines and identities. Golden failure never licenses editing its seal. Named diagnostics distinguish auth, permissions, copying and desktop proof.
lessons.surface: Machine selection source; Pack recovery sections; test-machine desktop reference.
lessons.gap: Zero-machine selection currently says only no test-machine capability. Proposed refusal should link the installed Pack/setup entry and supported choices, rather than force source search.
